newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Normandy sees more profit growth in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Normandy sees more profit growth in 97/98.

text.p: Gold miner Normandy Mining Ltd said on Monday it was still confident of achieving further profit growth in the year to June 30, 1998 despite the recent fall in the price of gold.

"We expect to achieve further profit growth in 1997/98, with gold again being the major contributor to group revenue and earnings," Robert Champion de Crespigny, the company's executive chairman said in a statement.

Champion de Crespigny said gold had driven Normandy to a record profit in the year to June 30, 1997 and the precious metal remained the group's priority despite the current price and the Reserve Bank of Australia's decision to sell 167 tonnes of its reserves over the past six months.
"We have positioned the Normandy business to counter periods of low gold prices, as will occur with all commodities from time to time," he said.
Normandy posted net earnings of A$42.2 million in the year to June 30, 1996.
Normandy completed a complex merger of its other listed mining associates, Gold Mines of Kalgoorlie Ltd and PosGold Ltd and a takeover bid for North Flinders Mines Ltd in December 1996.
Champion de Crespigny said the company's successful forward selling strategies would see the group realise a net gold price of over A$600 per ounce in the 1997/98 and 1998/99 financial years.
At 10.45 a.m (0045 GMT), Normandy shares were three cents weaker at A$1.38.
